AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Patients with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) often present with similar symptoms (chest pain, shortness of breath), similar electrocardiographic changes and elevated high-sensitivity troponin (cTn). It is not clear whether troponin reflects critical CAD or is elevated due to other causes in patients presenting with SVT. The aim of this study was to assess the role of elevated troponin in patients presenting with SVT.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for SVT and simultaneous coronary angiography at the Heart Centre Lucerne, Switzerland between January 2010 and October 2014 were included in this analysis. Significant CAD was defined as diameter-stenosis > 75% in vessels > 2.0 mm. The level of cTn was compared between patients with the presence or absence of CAD on coronary angiography. A cTn value of ≥ 0.014 µg/L was considered as elevated.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: During the study period a total of 473 patients underwent RFA for SVT. The study population consisted of 326 patients (69%, mean age 60 ± 12 years) who underwent invasive coronary angiography during the same session. The prevalence of significant CAD was 14% (45/326 patients). The highest prevalence of CAD was found in patients with atrial flutter (35%, 18/45 patients). cTn was elevated in 83% (10/12 patients) with significant CAD and in 47% (26/55 patients) without CAD.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The prevalence of CAD is low in patients with SVT, which questions the role of routine invasive coronary angiography during RFA. cTn measurement did not reliably exclude or confirm CAD in these patients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin does not indicate the presence of coronary artery disease in patients presenting with supraventricular tachycardia.
